To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

physiological levels of ascorbate are sufficient to maintain 5-hydroxmethylcytosine level in cellular DNA whereas higher concentrations of asocorbate are required to increase the level of 4 additional TET-mediated oxidation derivatives of 5-methlycytosine and of thymine.
ascorbate stimulates a moderate increase in 5- hydroxymethylcytocine content in cellular DNA, but a substantially larger increase in 5formylcytosine or 5-carboxylcytosine levels.
ascorbate enhances formation of all TET-mediated oxidation modifications of 5-methlycytosine and, for the first, time 5-hydroxyuracil.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first demonstration that ascorbate is a potent stimulator of 5-hydromethyluracil formation in human cells.
the role of ascorbate as a cofactor of TET proteins and its potential impact on DNA demethylation in human cells.
a novel function of ascorbate which is related to its participation in the TET-catalysed active demethylation process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ascorbate is a key player in regulation of DNA demethylation.

ascorbate stimulates formation of 5-formyl- and 5-carbocyctosine in cellular DNA and, for the first-time, we demonstrated that ascorbate is also capable of inducing formation of 5-mC-derived and TET-mediated 5-hydroxy- methyluracil.

vitamin C enhances substantially formation and/or stability of the active demethylation intermediate 5-hydroxy-methylcytosines in cellular DNA, and also stimulates the generation of 5-carboxy- and 5-formyl cytosines, as well as 5-hydro-xymethyluracils.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ascorbate is a key player in regulation of DNA methylation.
ascorbate is able to stimulate formation of all TET-mediated oxidation product of 5-mC, i.e., 5hmC, 5fC, 5caC, and 5hmU.

vitamin C, in physiological concentrations, may be a key player in active demethylation in human cells, while in higher concentrations, it may contribute to the generation of 5-formyl and 5-carbonyl derivatives of cytosine and uracil in cellular genomes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the TET-mediated demethylation process can be regulated by ascorbate.

the level of 4-oxo-2-nonenal (an endogenously generated electrophilic aldehyde), which is a known inhibitor of TET proteins, should be taken into account when studying the role of ascorbate on the level of 6-hydroxymethylation of DNA.
ascorbate, which is an essential nutrient for humans, may be a key factor that determines the level of 4-hydroxymethylation of DNA in cells.
